extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, researchers, and prospective workshop organizers/applicants to BIRS
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and constraints for proposing and running meetings at the Banff International Research Station (BIRS): describes meeting types, participant limits, application timeline, selection process, facilities, and audiovisual/recording policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research scope / subject areas BIRS supports
rubrics_metrics.description: "BIRS embraces all aspects of the mathematical, computational and statistical sciences from the most fundamental challenges of pure and applied mathematics, theoretical and applied computer science, statistics, and mathematical physics, to financial and industrial mathematics, as well as the mathematics of information technology, and the life sciences."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the topical remit for meetings and activities hosted at BIRS — broadly inclusive across pure/applied mathematics, theoretical/applied CS, statistics, mathematical physics, industrial/financial mathematics, IT-related mathematics, and life-science applications. Proposals should fall within these areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of meetings and allowed durations
rubrics_metrics.description: BIRS hosts five types of meetings: 5-Day Workshops; 2-Day Workshops; Focused Research Groups; Research in Teams; Summer Schools and Training Camps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each meeting type has typical durations and purposes: 5-Day Workshops are core program (5 days); 2-Day Workshops are weekend events; Focused Research Groups meet 1–2 weeks; Research in Teams meet 1–2 weeks; Summer Schools/training camps can be up to 14 days. Proposals must specify appropriate type and duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant limits by meeting type
rubrics_metrics.description: 5-Day Workshops: up to 42 participants (some have only 21 participants and share a week). 2-Day Workshops: typically ~25 people. Focused Research Groups: up to 8 people. Research in Teams: 2–4 people. Summer Schools and Training Camps: instructional meetings for up to 40 students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must conform to the participant-capacity expectations for the chosen meeting type; smaller formats (focused groups, research in teams) are for concentrated, small-team work while 5-day workshops are larger collaborative gatherings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timeline and program planning
rubrics_metrics.description: The core program of 5-day workshops is created two years in advance. Every summer, BIRS issues a Call for Proposals soliciting applications for workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective organizers should plan well ahead (applications in response to the summer Call for Proposals) because scheduling is done two years ahead; late planning risks missing available weeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition for weeks / selectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 48 weeks per year available for the core 5-day workshops; competition has grown (79 proposals for 2003 program, 168 proposals for 2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is competitive; proposers should expect many submissions per available week and should prepare strong proposals accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: peer review by international experts
rubrics_metrics.description: An extensive peer-review process by international experts culminates in the selection of the scientific program for a given year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific merit is evaluated via peer review; proposals are judged by international expert reviewers. Proposals should therefore emphasize scientific importance, clarity of goals, and likely impact to succeed in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application routing for summer schools and other meeting types
rubrics_metrics.description: Summer schools and training camps must apply through the same process as 5-day workshops. The other types of meetings are far less competitive, and may be applied for at any time, through the BIRS website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers of summer schools should submit via the Call for Proposals like 5-day workshops; organizers of 2-day workshops, focused research groups, or research-in-teams can apply outside the main Call and with potentially lower competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting facilities and on-site amenities
rubrics_metrics.description: BIRS occupies two buildings on the Banff Centre campus: Corbett Hall (residence with bedrooms, common lounge, small library, space for small teams) and TransCanada PipeLines Pavilion (administrative offices, two lecture rooms, smaller rooms for break-outs and research teams). As part of Banff Centre, BIRS researchers have full access to its amenities and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and participants can expect resident accommodation, lecture and breakout rooms, and access to broader Banff Centre services. The location is chosen to enable immersion by removing scientists from day-to-day life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated lecture capture and recording policy
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2012 BIRS installed a fully automated lecture capture system providing live streaming and video recording; video recordings are automatically posted on the BIRS website within a few minutes after a lecture ends. Use of the system is opt-in, decided by individual lecturers at the time of their lecture via a touchscreen panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lecturers control recording on a per-lecture basis (opt-in); the system uses high-quality cameras to ensure chalkboard material is visible and embedded microphones/audio processing capture both lecturer and audience questions. Organizers should inform speakers about the opt-in capture and potential immediate posting of recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and archival of recorded content
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent research videos recorded at BIRS are also available in the iTunes podcast directory; recordings are posted promptly on the BIRS website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded lectures may be widely disseminated and archived; proposers and speakers should consider openness and publicity of their talks when deciding whether to opt in to recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated research output / impact
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a wide range of research publications citing lectures, meetings and reports from BIRS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIRS-hosted activities have historically led to publications and reports; proposals that articulate expected scientific output or follow-up publications may be viewed favorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding sources supporting BIRS operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Banff International Research Station is funded by four governments: the federal government of Canada (NSERC), the provincial government of Alberta (Alberta Science and Research Authority), the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), and Mexico's National Science and Technology Council (CONACYT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge of funding partners may inform cross-border participation, eligibility expectations, and institutional affiliations; proposals should follow any sponsor-related requirements noted on the BIRS website.
